Messages.Author: Bloodgod
Messages.Body:
In article <3370l4$pj7@jadzia.CSOS.ORST.EDU>, kalem@CSOS.ORST.EDU (Donnie
Breeding) writes:

>1.  Do all vampires get a vote?

Only Primogens, Justicars and Princes that are in the player's ready area
whether tapped or untapped get to vote.  One vote for a Primogen, two for
a Prince and three for a Justicar.

>2.  If so, where does it say that?

Section 17.1 of the rulebook.

>3.  Do tapped vampires get a vote? (See #2)

Primogens, Princes, or Justicars get to vote whether they are tapped or
untapped as long as they are in the Methuselah's "Ready Area".

>4.  Is the card: Disputed Territory missing an icon?
	It looks, acts and plays like a political action.

It's a Political Action card.  Another one of the many errors discovered
so far.

Messages.Body:

>Only Primogens, Justicars and Princes that are in the player's ready area
>whether tapped or untapped get to vote.  One vote for a Primogen, two for
>a Prince and three for a Justicar.

So players don't get a vote?  Aren't they Methuselahs and aren't 
Methuselahs vampires?

Reading section 17.1 of the rules votes come from the following sources:
1) political action card starting vote is worth one vote
2) other political action cards can be used as votes instead of invoking
	their normal action
3) minion vampires (1 for primogen, 2 for prince, 3 for justicar)
4) Edge can be made into one vote

So in our learn-the-rules game we had the first vote go real fast as only
the person playing the political action card had vote, the one given by
the card.  We decided that was silly, and let Methuselahs vote after that.
Having the second vote be a bloodhunt vote got us even more confused.

I'm looking forward to the real rules being published one of these days.
I knew I was in trouble when the sample card in the little booklet didn't
match the actual card that I had.  Flavor text for the rule booklet:
	No, your other left

Messages.Author: William L. Houts
Messages.Body:
Donnie Breeding (kalem@CSOS.ORST.EDU) wrote:

:      1) Do all vampires in play get a vote?
   
     Each Political Card is worth one vote, and you may choose to cast 
     one vote for each Political Card in your hand rather than playing it
     for its particular effect (ie, if you hold "Autarkis Persecution",
     you may play it as a ballot during a vote called by another Methuselah.)
     
     NOTE:  Ordinarily, upon playing a card, one immediately draws from the 
            library in order to maintain one's hand size.  When playing 
            Political Cards as ballots in a vote, however, one waits until
            the end of the vote.

    Also, you get votes for certain ready vampires in your control.

	Princes may cast 1 vote.
        Primogen may cast 2 votes.
        Justicars may cast 3 votes.
    
    Finally, you may choose to relinquish the Edge in exchange for 1 vote.

:      2) If so; where does it say that?  (damn little book) :)

    Page 39.

:      3) If so; do tapped vampires get a vote? (see #2)

Yes. In order to cast their votes, Princes, Primogen and Justicars need only
be READY;  they need not be UNTAPPED.  (Page 39.)

:      4) Is the card: Disputed Territory missing an icon?
: 	It looks, acts and plays like a political action.

Yes, apparently.  It looks, acts and plays like a Political Card, as you say. 
And beyond that, it SAYS that it's a Political Card.  Barring a commandment 
from Justicar Tom Wylie of the WotC Clan, I think we can assume that it's a 
Political Card.

Messages.Author: William L. Houts
Messages.Body:
D.A. Kuder (dakuder@netcom.com) wrote:

: So players don't get a vote?  Aren't they Methuselahs and aren't 
: Methuselahs vampires?

NO. 

Methuselahs do not get votes per se.  Though the player-Methuselahs are 
vampires, the premise of the game is that Methuselahs do not sully their 
own hands with direct actions of this kind.  Methuselahs expend power 
and influence in various ways in order to make other, lesser vampires 
--their minions-- to do their bidding. 

This premise is borne out by the structure and rules of the game. The 
direct actions of the Methuselahs upon the game-world is represented by 
the Master Card Phase.  Only through the playing of Master cards may 
Methuselahs be said to directly meddling in the affairs of Kine and Kindred 
--their own controlled and uncontrolled vampires, or those of their 
opponents.

In order to cast a vote, a Methuselah must either have: 

	1.  The Edge
    	2.  A ready Prince, Primogen or Justicar.
        3.  A Political Card.

Messages.Author: Doug DeJulio
Messages.Body:
In article <338a58$idq@cyberspace.com>,
William L. Houts <abraxas@cyberspace.com> wrote:
>Donnie Breeding (kalem@CSOS.ORST.EDU) wrote:
>
>:      1) Do all vampires in play get a vote?
>   
>     Each Political Card is worth one vote, and you may choose to cast 
>     one vote for each Political Card in your hand rather than playing it
>     for its particular effect (ie, if you hold "Autarkis Persecution",
>     you may play it as a ballot during a vote called by another Methuselah.)

Nit:

The Methuselah who called the vote can't discard additional political
cards to get more votes.  Only the OTHER Methuselahs can do this.
Also, the political card that's played as an action *is* replaced
immediately (not that this gets you anything).  See section 17.1 of
the rules.

This means, any time you call for a vote you're taking a big risk --
other folks can pull "suprise votes" out of their hands, but you
can't.

--

I do not believe this interpretation is correct. I freely admit
that the rules are written this way. I think that is in error.

My evidence for that is skimpy I admit and would love an official
ruling.

However, I believe that the Methuselah who called the vote CAN add
political cards to get more votes:

Why?

1) I was taught that way by WotC at Dragon CON
2) It makes sense that all Methuselahs are treated the same.
3) In the FAQ the following two questions are answered in a row:

Does the vote on the vote card count towards my referendum?
     Yes, when you call a vote, the card itself is worth one vote.

If I throw in another card from my hand for one vote, do I replace it
right away?
     (Sec. 17.1, "Voting")  No.  No cards get replaced until the vote
     is concluded.

It seems to imply in the second question that the the person throwing
in another vote is the player calling for a vote.

I admit my evidence is not that strong. BUT i would suggest players
allow the  Methuselah calling a vote to play additional vote cards
until WotC officially rules.

Both versions of the rulebook say that only ready vampires will grant
votes via their title (section 17.1).  This means that vampires in
torpor will not grant you votes.  This becomes very important when
diablerizing them  ;)

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
I checked, and the Methuselah calling a vote can indeed burn political
cards to gain more votes.  I'm not sure how one is supposed to figure
this out from the rules, but there you go.  Remember that cards burned
during a vote are not replaced until the vote is over (though the action
card which led to the vote would have been replaced immediately).

Messages.Author: Matt Rollefson

In rec.games.deckmaster aahz@hal.COM (Tom Wylie) writes:
>I checked, and the Methuselah calling a vote can indeed burn political
>cards to gain more votes.  I'm not sure how one is supposed to figure
>this out from the rules, but there you go.  Remember that cards burned
>during a vote are not replaced until the vote is over (though the action
>card which led to the vote would have been replaced immediately).

Well, it's very fuzzy, but this is what they say (section 17.1):

"A political card always provides on vote for the Methuselah playing
it. ... Additional political cards can also be used by any of the
other Methuselahs for votes."

The "also" suggests to me that the Methuselah calling the vote can
certainly use additional cards, and that they're adding this sentence
to make sure it's understood that the other Methuselah's can as well,
even though they're action cards and not normally playable out of
turn. Granted, this is wide open to interpretation, but at least the
ruling is consistent with the rules.

Rollie

Messages.Author: Merrill Brick
Messages.Body:
David Kiker (kdk@template.com) wrote:
: In article <338r2p$csc@usenet.srv.cis.pitt.edu>, ddj@zardoz.elbows.org (Doug DeJulio) writes:

Apparently, Donnie, all those who responded to your question were 
confusing the term "vampire" in your question with Methuselah.  
Methuselahs, including the one who called the vote, can play political 
cards worth one vote apiece, tap Ventrue Headquarters for three votes, 
and various other vote-casting cards.  As for "vampires", properly termed 
*minions* to avoid said confusion, the votes go like this:
Primogens -------------1 vote
Princes----------------2 votes
Justicars--------------3 votes
Any minion without any of these three titles do NOT get votes.



Note:  Contested titles and/or contested, titled minions
receive NO vote at all as they are not controlled yet by any Methuselah.
As such, Princes cannot vote on their own Praxis.
